metadata.title: The Double Slit: How Far Apart Are the Stripes? (Worked Example)
metadata.thing: two slits and a screen; the de Broglie wavelength lambda=h/p turned into a measurable fringe spacing delta-y = lambda L / d, worked for a 100 eV electron
metadata.color_notes: Slits/screen/axes = ink #1a1a1a. Waves + fringe curve + boxed formula = accent #5A5653. The final fringe-spacing answer = red #C0392B. Math is MathTex (LaTeX).
metadata.math_rendering: MathTex (LaTeX, MacTeX). de Broglie: lambda[nm] = 1.226/sqrt(V). 100 V -> 0.123 nm. d=100nm, L=0.5m -> dy=0.61mm.

Bear's Notes

beats.tts_normalized_text:

beats.new_visual_element: title card: brand + slits-and-fringes motif + title

beats.narration_text: One electron at a time still piles up into stripes — interference with itself.
beats.tts_normalized_text: One electron at a time still piles up into stripes — interference with itself.

beats.narration_text: And the spacing of those stripes is something we can predict.
beats.tts_normalized_text: And the spacing of those stripes is something we can predict.
beats.new_visual_element: narration card + a delta-y bracket on fringes

beats.narration_text: Each electron's wave passes through both slits and overlaps on the far side.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Each electron's wave passes through both slits and overlaps on the far side.
beats.new_visual_element: two slits, waves spreading and overlapping

beats.narration_text: Bright fringes land where the two paths differ by a whole wavelength.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Bright fringes land where the two paths differ by a whole wavelength.
beats.new_visual_element: two path lines to a bright fringe
geometry on the left, math on the right

beats.narration_text: A particle's wavelength is de Broglie's — lambda equals h over p.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A particle's wavelength is de Broglie's — lambda equals h over p.

beats.narration_text: Bright fringes sit where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Bright fringes sit where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths.

beats.narration_text: For small angles that spaces the stripes by delta-y equals lambda L over d.
beats.tts_normalized_text: For small angles that spaces the stripes by delta y equals lambda L over d.
beats.new_visual_element: boxed result delta-y = lambda L / d

beats.narration_text: Take an electron pushed through one hundred volts.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Take an electron pushed through one hundred volts.
beats.new_visual_element: boxed formula at top; givens: 100 V electron

beats.narration_text: Its momentum gives a wavelength of about zero point one two nanometres.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Its momentum gives a wavelength of about zero point one two nanometres.

beats.narration_text: Set the slits one hundred nanometres apart, the screen half a metre away.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Set the slits one hundred nanometres apart, the screen half a metre away.
beats.new_visual_element: d and L marked on the geometry

beats.narration_text: The stripes come out about zero point six millimetres apart — easily seen.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The stripes come out about zero point six millimetres apart — easily seen.

beats.narration_text: Speed the electron up, its wavelength shrinks, and the stripes crowd closer.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Speed the electron up, its wavelength shrinks, and the stripes crowd closer.
beats.new_visual_element: two fringe patterns: wide vs tight

beats.narration_text: This is exactly what Tonomura saw in 1989 — dots, one by one, building the fringes.
beats.tts_normalized_text: This is exactly what Tonomura saw in 1989 — dots, one by one, building the fringes.

beats.narration_text: The stripe spacing is just the electron's wavelength, made visible.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The stripe spacing is just the electron's wavelength, made visible.

beats.narration_text: Random alone, lawful together — the wave sets the odds.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Random alone, lawful together — the wave sets the odds.
